sources.entry: gadak - Keeps Jira, Linear and Confluence in one local SQLite file you query with SQL, and is a tracker of its own with no account.

summary.one_liner: gadak mirrors selected Jira Cloud projects and Confluence spaces into one local SQLite file that you can query with SQL, browse in a desktop app or browser, script from a CLI, or expose over MCP.
summary.what_it_does: It syncs the Jira Cloud projects and Confluence spaces you choose (issues, comments, history, wiki pages) into a single SQLite database on your machine, indexed for offline search. You can read that mirror through a desktop app, a browser tab via `gadak serve`, the CLI, or MCP. Ad hoc SQL such as GROUP BY counts runs against the local file, which JQL cannot express. Writes (create, edit, comment, transition and similar) go to Jira first, and the mirror refreshes after Jira accepts them. The README also describes support for Jira Server/Data Center and Linear origins, a built-in tracker, and an iOS app in beta. Agents can read the mirror through a shipped skill or MCP registration.
use_cases: offline search of Jira and Confluence
give a coding agent read access to a Jira mirror
faster Jira list and search than the REST API
how_to_run: gadak sql "select epic_key, count(*) from issues_full where resolved_at is null and epic_key <> '' group by epic_key order by 2 desc"
notable: Single binary and single SQLite file mirror that can be deleted and rebuilt without loss
Writes go through the origin first; rejected writes fail immediately and nothing is queued
Same verbs across Atlassian Cloud, Jira Server/Data Center, Linear and a built-in tracker
Agent skill install for Claude Code and other hosts, plus MCP registration
Benchmarks published against a live Cloud site, with cases where gadak is slower documented
caveats: Status is 0.x with a single maintainer; compatibility promised only for a few listed items
First full sync is slow (3.7 minutes for the benchmark site) and reads lag Jira by up to one sync interval (60 seconds default)
Sprint UI, Jira dashboards and notification inbox stay in Jira and are not available on any origin; iOS app is beta via TestFlight only
Windows desktop zip is unsigned; Microsoft Store install is the signed route
